title: A dynamic phospho-switch that times diurnal stomatal movements in Arabidopsis
content: Plants, like other organisms, live according to a daily rhythm. Stomatal movements are crucial for plant photosynthesis and water use efficiency (WUE). Light is the central factor regulating stomatal movements, and stomatal apertures exhibit diurnal changes in response to the light/dark cycle, with substantial evidence showing that blue and red light induce stomatal opening. ROP GUANINE NUCLEOTIDE EXCHANGE FACTOR 2 (RopGEF2) catalyzes the exchange of RHO OF PLANTS (ROPs) from the inactive GDP- to the active GTP-bound form in guard cells (Fig. 1). PhyB activates this pathway to suppress red light–induced stomatal opening (Wang et al. 2017). However, how RopGEF2 activity is regulated in guard cells under different light conditions remains poorly understood, and it is still unclear whether this regulation contributes to the fine-tuning of stomatal apertures during diurnal stomatal movement. In addition, protein phosphorylation and protein kinases also play an important role in stomatal movements. RopGEFs are subject to phosphorylation, which influences their localization, activity, and/or degradation. Moreover, MPK3 and MPK6, 2 key protein kinases, are essential for stomatal closure induced by UV-B, ethylene, and bacteria (Li et al. 2017; Zhang et al. 2021; Zhang et al. 2024). However, it remains unclear whether MPK3 and MPK6 are activated by white light (WL) in guard cells and whether they participate in the regulation of stomatal apertures during diurnal stomatal movements through phosphorylation of key components in guard cell signaling.
